assessments.explanation: Ms. Yani Meilina, a citizen of Indonesia, seeks judicial review of a decision dismissing her refugee claim and findings about internal flight alternative.
The RAD applied the reasonableness standard to the RPD's findings, and the issue is whether this was correct.
The respondent argues that even if the RAD erred, the outcome would be the same under the correctness standard, so the application should be dismissed.
The court disagrees with the respondent, stating that if the RAD erred, the application should be granted and the matter remitted for a new decision.
The paragraph explains the standards of review for legal errors, including when correctness or reasonableness applies, citing relevant case law.
The court discusses jurisprudence on the standard of review, noting that some cases favor correctness for legal questions of general interest.
The court expresses disagreement with applying correctness to the interpretation of RAD provisions, viewing it as a question of specific statutory interpretation.
The court concludes that the choice of standard does not affect the outcome, as the same conclusion would be reached under either standard.
The court notes that further issues regarding deference and scope of questions of fact will be addressed by the FCA.
The court finds the applicant was denied proper appeal rights, quashes the RAD decision, and remits the case for re-determination.
The court certifies a question about whether the RAD owes deference to RPD findings within its statutory framework.
The court grants the application, sets aside the RAD decision, remits the case, and certifies the key legal question.
